segments: ...a woollen girdle {OCR?} they should bind around their heads;
and without girdles and zunnars, not one of them should be seen outside.
And if any of them had a slave,
he should sew two patches of different colours on his tunic, in front and behind;
and that their new churches should be demolished;
and if they had a spacious church,
even if it were old,
a portion of it should be made into a mosque;
and that they should not raise crosses {OCR: ܨܠܝ̈ܒܐ} on their Palm Sundays.
These and many tyrannical commands like these
he likewise imposed upon the Jews.
And furthermore, he demolished the tomb of Husayn, the son of Ali, who was descended from the daughter of their prophet;
and he also tore down the other houses around it;
and he ploughed with a team of oxen and sowed crops in that place,
so that the site of the tomb would be completely obliterated.
And in his days there appeared a certain man in Nishapur who said of himself that he was a prophet,
and he made for himself a book containing, as he claimed, the words which the angel Gabriel had spoken with him;
and many followed him.
And when he was seized and scourged,
he confessed his imposture.
And in his third year, he set his three sons over the lands:

al-Muntasir over Africa, Egypt, Mesopotamia, Assyria, the Khabur, Circesium, Tagrit, the South, and the land of Sheba and Seba as far as the border of India, and Shahrazur, Isfahan, Qom, Kashan, Qazvin, and all the mountains of Persia;
and over al-Mu'tazz, his second son, he gave authority over Khorasan, Tabaristan, Rayy, Armenia, and Azerbaijan,
and that he should receive the revenue account of the entire dominion of the Arabs in general;
and over al-Mu'ayyad, his third son, he gave authority over Damascus, Homs, the land of the Jordan, and Palestine.
And in the year 237 [of the Arabs] [A.D. 851/2],
(237 of the Arabs?) Bagrat, son of Ashot, the patrician of Armenia, when he came to Yusuf, son of Muhammad, the general of the Arabs, for the sake of peace,
he seized him and sent him in chains to Baghdad.
Then the armies of the Romans and of the Armenians gathered against the city of Taron, in which Yusuf was.
And when he went out against them to fight,
he and all the warriors who were with him were killed.
